report.source_text: By day 4 of IV vancomycin treatment, the patient’s rash and pruritus had not improved, causing him significant emotional distress. Due to concern of drug reaction to vancomycin, antibiotics were changed to IV cefazolin given his limited autoimmune markers and lack of response to anti-bacterial agents, and he was started on prednisone 60 mg PO and topical Triamcinolone 0.1% cream applied copiously and faithfully BID.

clinician.trajectory_summary: 56-year-old man presented with diffuse desquamative rash involving face, torso, and extremities with characteristic sparing of palms, soles, and mucosa, following recurrent GAS skin infections and multiple antibiotic exposures (Augmentin, Clindamycin, Bactrim). Initial presentation included systemic symptoms (tachycardia 130 bpm, hypertension 158/116 mmHg, tachypnea 22 bpm) and laboratory abnormalities (leukocytosis 17.9 thou/mm3, azotemia BUN 24 mg/dL). Skin biopsy of the dorsum of the right hand revealed psoriasiform hyperplasia with atypical T cell infiltrate and eosinophils. TCR gene rearrangement studies from University of Michigan Dermatopathology showed no clonal cells, ruling out cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Initial treatment with IV vancomycin failed by day 4 with persistent rash and pruritus. After switching to IV cefazolin and initiating prednisone 60mg PO daily plus topical triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID, the patient showed progressive improvement with complete resolution of desquamation and erythema by day 12 of therapy.
